edits.old: For a distribution $u$ on a smooth manifold, the chartwise rapid-decay definition of its wavefront set is independent of the chart: if $y=\psi(x)$, its covector coordinates satisfy $\eta=(D\psi(x))^{-T}\xi$. The resulting $\operatorname{WF}(u)$ is closed and conic in $T^*M\setminus0$. For distributions $u,v$ and a smooth diffeomorphism $\psi$, one has $\operatorname{WF}(u+v)\subseteq\operatorname{WF}(u)\cup\operatorname{WF}(v)$ and $\operatorname{WF}(\psi^*u)=\psi^*\operatorname{WF}(u)$. Finally, $\operatorname{WF}(u)=\varnothing$ exactly when $u$ is represented by a smooth scalar function in every chart.

edits.new: [F3] [[lem-qftx-microcausal-star-product]]: $\star_W$ is defined coefficientwise on the stated microcausal polynomial class by finitely many Hadamard contractions and preserves that class. Separately, [[def-qftx-local-time-ordered-system]] assumes $W-W^{\mathsf T}=iE$ for a fixed $E$ supported on causal pairs; this is a premise of the free datum, not a conclusion of the contraction lemma.

edits.old: 6.1 Each graph ambiguity space at a fixed field and jet order is finite-dimensional because the allowed derivative order is finite. Work on its balanced-label module; the total/relative derivative splitting [F11] is Lorentz equivariant, so the following correction on balanced labels extends by differentiation without spoiling representation independence. For a graph let $c(X)=X\cdot T_n^1$ be the infinitesimal Lorentz variation of the chosen extension. Since the off-diagonal graph data are Lorentz invariant, $c(X)$ vanishes off $\Delta_n$ and lies in that finite-dimensional local jet space. The representation law gives the cocycle identity $c([X,Y])=\rho(X)c(Y)-\rho(Y)c(X)$. By [F9] there is a local jet $v$ with $c(X)=\rho(X)v$; replacing the extension by $T_n^1-v$ makes its infinitesimal defect zero. The proper-orthochronous group is connected, so invariance along every smooth path from the identity gives full $SO^+(1,3)$ covariance. Translation covariance already holds by the relative-coordinate lift. [F1, F8, F9, F11, step 5.1, algebra]
edits.new:
6.1 Keep together all components that mix under Lorentz transformations. At fixed input field degrees and homogeneous derivative degrees, take the finite-dimensional space $L$ of balanced input-label tensors and the finite-dimensional space $O$ of remaining field-jet labels occurring in their finite graph expansion, enlarging each to contain its full Lorentz orbit. The substitution $p_a\mapsto\Lambda^{\mathsf T}p_a$ of [F11] defines their representations $R_L,R_O$; linear substitutions preserve field degree and homogeneous derivative degree, so these enlargements remain finite. In relative dimension $d=4(n-1)$ put $A_\Lambda(z_1,\ldots,z_{n-1})=(\Lambda z_1,\ldots,\Lambda z_{n-1})$ and $U_\Lambda=(A_{\Lambda^{-1}})^*\otimes R_O(\Lambda)$ on $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^d)\otimes O$. Regard the chosen numerical coefficients collectively as $t^1\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(L,\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^d)\otimes O)$, with combined action $(\Lambda\cdot t)(b)=U_\Lambda t(R_L(\Lambda)^{-1}b)$. These are representations by the pullback and substitution laws. On the punctured relative space the collective coefficient $t^0$ is fixed by this combined action: the free kernels are invariant, their differentiated components transform by the chain rule, and the already covariant lower-order products agree on the causal-cover overlaps. A fixed coordinate derivative component need not be scalar invariant. [F1, F11, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

7.1 For the finite block in step 6.1 choose a common finite engineering upper bound $B$ compatible with its homogeneous label degrees and the finitely many lower-order counterterms. Linear coordinate changes commute with positive dilations and preserve these bounds. Put $J_N=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{\partial^\alpha\delta_0:|\alpha|\le N\}$, where $N=\lfloor B-d\rfloor$ when $B\ge d$, and put $J_N=0$ when $B<d$. The permitted local corrections form the invariant subspace $V$ of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(L,J_N\otimes O)$ satisfying the labelwise engineering bounds and the linear identities of the balanced coefficients. This space is finite-dimensional. Lorentz substitutions preserve each homogeneous degree and delta-derivative order, while [F11] makes the derivative identities equivariant, proving invariance of this subspace. Differentiate the combined action to obtain $\rho(X)$ and put $c(X)=\rho(X)t^1$. Restriction commutes with the action, and step 6.1 gives $\rho(X)t^0=0$, so $c(X)$ is supported at the relative origin. It obeys the same engineering bounds and identities; [F8] and [F10] therefore place it in $V$. Smooth differentiation is justified by differentiating the transformed compact test densities in their fixed-support smooth topology; the finite-order distribution bound then permits pairing. The representation law gives $c([X,Y])=\rho(X)c(Y)-\rho(Y)c(X)$, so $c:\mathfrak{so}(1,3)\to V$ is exactly a real-linear cocycle in the finite-dimensional complex module required by [F9]. [F8, F9, F10, F11, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 Apply [F9] to this module and cocycle to obtain $v\in V$ with $c(X)=\rho(X)v$. Thus $t^1-v$ has zero infinitesimal combined defect, retains the engineering bounds, and agrees with $t^0$ off the diagonal. Its combined orbit is constant along each one-parameter subgroup by the preceding smooth test-pairing argument. Along a smooth group path $g(s)$ the orbit derivative is the transported infinitesimal action of $g(s)^{-1}g'(s)$ and hence is zero. In the identity component every point is reachable by a piecewise smooth path: the set reachable from the identity and its complement are open, using straight paths in coordinate balls. Connectedness therefore gives full $SO^+(1,3)$ covariance. Work separately in homogeneous balanced-label degrees, whose finite spaces are Lorentz invariant, and recover total-derivative descendants by [F11]; the resulting corrections are compatible on their algebraic direct sum and preserve representation independence. The choices of these finite-block corrections are permitted by [A1]. Translation covariance is retained because every correction is a relative delta jet lifted by the same center-coordinate integral as in step 5.1. [A1, F1, F8, F9, F11, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, algebra]
